title: Chapter 9: Multi-Step and Multi-Agent Workflows
content:
Chapter 9: Multi-Step and Multi-Agent Workflows

Give Each Step a Clear Job

A longer AI task often involves several kinds of work: deciding what to cover, organising notes, writing a draft and checking it. Separating those jobs can make the result easier to inspect. It also adds API calls, waiting time and more places for errors to enter the process, so each extra step needs a purpose.

In this chapter, you will build a Research and Summary Agent. It uses five roles in a fixed sequence: planner, researcher, writer, reviewer and reviser. Starting with a topic, the workflow creates a plan and notes, drafts a brief, critiques it and revises it. You will save each stage so that you can trace a weak final answer back to the step that needs attention.

What You Will Learn

  • Distinguish a multi-step workflow from a system that delegates work among agents.
  • Assign responsibilities to the planner, researcher, writer, reviewer and reviser, then pass their outputs between steps.
  • Decide when extra roles justify their cost and when a single call or ordinary Python is enough.
  • Save intermediate results for debugging and mark claims that need outside verification.
  • Build the workflow in Python, test its formatting without API calls, and adapt it to writing, study, business and automation tasks.

Connecting the Earlier Projects

You have already worked with LLM calls, command-line apps, RAG, semantic search, tools, memory and workflow automation. This chapter adds role-based decomposition: dividing a broad request into smaller jobs with distinct instructions.

Consider this prompt:

Research Python AI agents and write a polished article.

It leaves the model to decide what research, writing and checking should involve. A staged workflow makes those responsibilities explicit:

  • Planner: create a research plan.
  • Researcher: create careful notes and mark uncertain claims.
  • Writer: turn notes into a structured brief.
  • Reviewer: identify weak claims, gaps, and unclear sections.
  • Reviser: improve the final brief.

If the result disappoints you, inspect the hand-offs. A vague plan can produce vague notes; a writer can omit a useful point; a reviewer can overlook an unsupported claim; and a reviser can overstate a conclusion. Separating the stages gives you somewhere specific to investigate.

9.1 What Is a Multi-Step Workflow?

A multi-step workflow runs a sequence of tasks, each with a defined input and output. In this project the sequence is:

  1. Input topic
  2. Plan
  3. Research notes
  4. Draft
  5. Review
  6. Final output

Each output feeds the next step. One assistant using different prompts could carry out the whole sequence; the structure does not, by itself, require several independent agents.

9.2 What Is a Multi-Agent Workflow?

A multi-agent workflow assigns different responsibilities to AI components, with a separate instruction for each role.

RoleJob
PlannerDecide what needs to be covered
ResearcherGather or organize notes
WriterCreate the draft
ReviewerCritique the draft
ReviserImprove the final result

Here, the agents use the same LLM client with different prompts. This lets you learn how to separate responsibilities without introducing an agent framework. The distinction between roles matters more to this project than the number of model instances.

9.3 Workflow vs Multi-Agent System

The terms overlap. For this chapter, use the following distinction to describe how much control the application keeps over the sequence.

PatternMeaningExample
WorkflowA fixed sequence of stepsPlan → Write → Review
Multi-agent workflowA workflow where each step has a rolePlanner → Researcher → Writer → Reviewer
Fully autonomous agent systemAgents decide more of the process themselvesAgent chooses tools, delegates, loops, stops

You will build a controlled workflow with a fixed order. That makes the sequence easier to follow and debug while you learn how the roles interact.

9.4 Why Use Multiple Roles?

Planning, writing and reviewing need different instructions. The planner explores the topic's scope; the researcher organises cautious notes; and the writer concentrates on an understandable brief. The reviewer then looks for weaknesses, while the reviser responds to that feedback without introducing unsupported claims.

Separate prompts give each call a narrower task. They can help you tune one stage without changing all the others, although assigning roles does not guarantee that the model will follow them well.

9.5 The Limits of This Research Workflow

Despite its name, the Research and Summary Agent does not browse the web. Its researcher organises the model's existing knowledge and marks claims that need verification. It cannot check current facts without suitable external evidence.

Use the output for brainstorming, planning, drafts, study notes, content outlines and first-pass internal briefs. It is insufficient on its own for legal research, medical advice, financial decisions, breaking news, academic citations, current market claims or publication of factual statistics.

The prompts instruct the model to identify uncertainty. You still need to check claims against trusted sources before relying on or publishing them. A reviewer model can flag a doubtful statement, but its approval is not factual verification.

9.6 Project: Research and Summary Agent

Project Outputs

For each topic, the application produces a research plan, research notes, a first draft, review comments and a revised brief. A Markdown report holds all five stages together.

Where You Might Use It

The workflow offers a starting structure for student study briefs, article planning, freelance summaries, product exploration and internal briefing documents. For developers, it is also a small example of how to organise calls and inspect the material passed between them.

"""Small, lazily connected LLM client; importing the project needs no API key."""

import math
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from openai import OpenAI, OpenAIError


def get_env_float(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    """Use the default for missing, malformed or non-finite values."""
    try:
        value = float(os.getenv(name, str(default)))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default
    return value if math.isfinite(value) else default


@dataclass
class LLMConfig:
    model: str = field(default_factory=lambda: os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4.1-mini"))
    temperature: float = field(default_factory=lambda: get_env_float("OPENAI_TEMPERATURE", 0.2))


class LLMClient:
    """Use complete(system, user); inject an SDK-compatible client for offline tests."""

    def __init__(self, config: LLMConfig | None = None, *, client=None):
        load_dotenv(override=False)
        self.config = config or LLMConfig()
        if not self.config.model.strip():
            raise ValueError("Model cannot be empty.")
        if not math.isfinite(self.config.temperature) or not 0 <= self.config.temperature <= 2:
            raise ValueError("Temperature must be a finite number between 0 and 2.")
        self.client = client

    def complete(self, system: str, user: str) -> str:
        """Return nonempty output, or raise a clear error without echoing secrets."""
        if not isinstance(system, str) or not system.strip():
            raise ValueError("System instruction cannot be empty.")
        if not isinstance(user, str) or not user.strip():
            raise ValueError("User request cannot be empty.")
        if self.client is None:
            api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip()
            if not api_key or api_key == "replace_with_your_api_key":
                raise ValueError("OPENAI_API_KEY is missing. Add it to your private .env file.")
            self.client = OpenAI(api_key=api_key, timeout=30.0, max_retries=2)
        try:
            response = self.client.responses.create(
                model=self.config.model,
                instructions=system.strip(),
                input=user.strip(),
                temperature=self.config.temperature,
            )
        except OpenAIError:
            raise RuntimeError("The model request failed. Check connectivity, credentials and provider status.") from None
        output = getattr(response, "output_text", None)
        if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
            raise RuntimeError("The model returned no usable text; no result was completed.")
        return output.strip()

"""
Prompt builders for the Chapter 9 Research and Summary Agent.
"""
PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a careful research planner.
Your job is to turn a topic into a clear research plan.
Do not write the final brief.
Do not invent statistics.
Focus on useful questions, subtopics, assumptions, and risks.
"""
RESEARCHER_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a cautious research note taker.
Your job is to create structured research notes based on the provided plan.
Do not pretend to browse the web.
Do not invent statistics, citations, or sources.
Mark any claim that needs verification.
Use careful language.
"""
WRITER_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a clear technical and business writer.
Your job is to turn research notes into a structured brief.
Write for beginner-to-intermediate readers.
Be practical, clear, and organized.
Do not add unsupported facts.
"""
REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a strict editor and factual-risk reviewer.
Your job is to review a draft for:
- Unsupported claims
- Vague wording
- Missing context
- Overpromising
- Confusing structure
- Claims that need verification
Be direct and practical.
"""
REVISER_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are a careful reviser.
Your job is to improve a draft using reviewer feedback.
Do not add unsupported facts.
Do not add fake citations.
Keep the final brief clear, useful, and careful.
"""
def build_planner_prompt(topic: str) -> str:
    """Build the planner prompt."""
    return f"""
Create a research plan for this topic:
{topic}
Return:
1. Main research goal
2. Key questions to answer
3. Important subtopics
4. Target reader
5. Practical use cases
6. Risks, assumptions, or unclear areas
7. Suggested final brief structure
Important:
This is only a plan. Do not write the full brief yet.
"""
def build_researcher_prompt(topic: str, plan: str) -> str:
    """Build the researcher prompt."""
    return f"""
Topic:
{topic}
Research plan:
{plan}
Create structured research notes.
Return:
1. Key concepts
2. Important context
3. Practical examples
4. Potential benefits
5. Potential risks or limitations
6. Claims that need verification
7. Suggested angles for the final brief
Important:
- Do not pretend you browsed the web.
- Do not invent statistics.
- Do not invent citations.
- Mark uncertain or current claims as "Needs verification."
"""
def build_writer_prompt(topic: str, research_notes: str) -> str:
    """Build the writer prompt."""
    return f"""
Topic:
{topic}
Research notes:
{research_notes}
Write a structured brief.
Use this format:
# Brief Title
## Executive Summary
## Why This Matters
## Key Ideas
## Practical Use Cases
## Risks and Limitations
## Actionable Recommendations
## Claims to Verify Before Publication
Important:
- Use clear language.
- Do not invent facts.
- Do not include fake citations.
- Keep the brief practical.
"""
def build_reviewer_prompt(draft: str) -> str:
    """Build the reviewer prompt."""
    return f"""
Review the following draft:
{draft}
Return:
1. Strongest parts
2. Weakest parts
3. Unsupported or risky claims
4. Vague sections
5. Missing reader context
6. Suggested improvements
7. Final recommendation: publish, revise, or verify further
Be strict but constructive.
"""
def build_reviser_prompt(draft: str, review: str) -> str:
    """Build the reviser prompt."""
    return f"""
Original draft:
{draft}
Reviewer feedback:
{review}
Revise the draft.
Rules:
- Improve clarity and structure.
- Remove or soften unsupported claims.
- Keep "Claims to Verify Before Publication" if needed.
- Do not invent sources or statistics.
- Keep the final version practical and publication-friendly.
"""

"""Five roles using separate prompts and an optional shared client."""

from llm_client import LLMClient
from prompts import (
    PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    RESEARCHER_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    WRITER_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    REVISER_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    build_planner_prompt,
    build_researcher_prompt,
    build_writer_prompt,
    build_reviewer_prompt,
    build_reviser_prompt,
)


def planner_agent(topic: str, *, client=None) -> str:
    client = client if client is not None else LLMClient()
    return client.complete(system=PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user=build_planner_prompt(topic))


def researcher_agent(topic: str, plan: str, *, client=None) -> str:
    client = client if client is not None else LLMClient()
    return client.complete(system=RESEARCHER_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user=build_researcher_prompt(topic, plan))


def writer_agent(topic: str, research_notes: str, *, client=None) -> str:
    client = client if client is not None else LLMClient()
    return client.complete(system=WRITER_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user=build_writer_prompt(topic, research_notes))


def reviewer_agent(draft: str, *, client=None) -> str:
    client = client if client is not None else LLMClient()
    return client.complete(system=REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user=build_reviewer_prompt(draft))


def reviser_agent(draft: str, review: str, *, client=None) -> str:
    client = client if client is not None else LLMClient()
    return client.complete(system=REVISER_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user=build_reviser_prompt(draft, review))

9.12 File: workflow.py

"""Run the five fixed roles; their outputs remain unverified model drafts."""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from agents import planner_agent, researcher_agent, writer_agent, reviewer_agent, reviser_agent
from llm_client import LLMClient


@dataclass
class ResearchWorkflowResult:
    topic: str
    plan: str
    research_notes: str
    draft: str
    review: str
    final_brief: str


def validate_topic(topic: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(topic, str):
        raise ValueError("Topic must be text.")
    cleaned = topic.strip()
    if not cleaned:
        raise ValueError("Topic cannot be empty.")
    if len(cleaned) > 300:
        raise ValueError("Topic is too long for this beginner demo.")
    return cleaned


def _require_stage_text(stage: str, output: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
        raise RuntimeError(f"{stage} returned no usable text; the workflow stopped.")
    return output.strip()


def run_research_workflow(topic: str, *, client=None) -> ResearchWorkflowResult:
    """Reuse one client; stop immediately if a stage fails or returns empty text."""
    cleaned_topic = validate_topic(topic)
    client = client if client is not None else LLMClient()

    print("Step 1/5: Planning...")
    plan = _require_stage_text("Planner", planner_agent(cleaned_topic, client=client))
    print("Step 2/5: Creating research notes...")
    research_notes = _require_stage_text(
        "Researcher", researcher_agent(topic=cleaned_topic, plan=plan, client=client)
    )
    print("Step 3/5: Writing draft brief...")
    draft = _require_stage_text(
        "Writer", writer_agent(topic=cleaned_topic, research_notes=research_notes, client=client)
    )
    print("Step 4/5: Reviewing draft...")
    review = _require_stage_text("Reviewer", reviewer_agent(draft, client=client))
    print("Step 5/5: Revising final brief...")
    final_brief = _require_stage_text(
        "Reviser", reviser_agent(draft=draft, review=review, client=client)
    )
    return ResearchWorkflowResult(cleaned_topic, plan, research_notes, draft, review, final_brief)

9.13 File: report_writer.py

"""Save every workflow stage to a local, explicitly unverified Markdown report."""

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

from workflow import ResearchWorkflowResult


def slugify(text: str, max_length: int = 60) -> str:
    """Create a filename-friendly slug; collapse adjacent separator characters."""
    if not isinstance(max_length, int) or isinstance(max_length, bool) or max_length < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_length must be a positive integer.")
    allowed = []
    for character in text.lower():
        if character.isalnum():
            allowed.append(character)
        elif character in {" ", "-", "_"}:
            allowed.append("_")
    slug = "_".join(part for part in "".join(allowed).split("_") if part)
    return (slug or "research_brief")[:max_length]


def build_markdown_report(result: ResearchWorkflowResult) -> str:
    return f"""# Research Workflow Report

> Status: Unverified model draft. No human approval has been recorded.
> A model review is not factual verification or permission to publish.

## Topic

{result.topic}

---

## 1. Research Plan

{result.plan}

---

## 2. Research Notes

{result.research_notes}

---

## 3. Draft Brief

{result.draft}

---

## 4. Reviewer Feedback

{result.review}

---

## 5. Final Revised Brief

{result.final_brief}

---

## Important Verification Note

This workflow does not browse the web or verify current facts by itself.
Review factual claims, statistics, legal claims, medical claims, financial claims,
and current events before publication or professional use.
All five stages remain model-generated drafts, including a reviewer recommendation
to publish. This report does not record a human approval decision.
"""


def save_report(result: ResearchWorkflowResult, output_dir: str = "outputs") -> Path:
    """Create nested directories and a new report; never overwrite an older run."""
    output_path = Path(output_dir)
    output_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S_%fZ")
    file_path = output_path / f"{timestamp}_{slugify(result.topic)}_{uuid4().hex[:8]}.md"
    with file_path.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as report_file:
        report_file.write(build_markdown_report(result))
    return file_path

9.14 File: app.py

"""Chapter 9: Planner → Researcher → Writer → Reviewer → Reviser."""

from report_writer import save_report
from workflow import run_research_workflow


def main(*, client=None, output_dir: str = "outputs") -> int:
    print("\nResearch and Summary Agent")
    print("=" * 45)
    print("This workflow creates a plan, notes, draft, review, and final brief.")
    print("It does not verify current facts or browse the web.")
    print("=" * 45)
    try:
        topic = input("\nEnter research topic: ").strip()
    except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
        print("\nCancelled.")
        return 0
    if not topic:
        print("No topic provided.")
        return 0
    try:
        result = run_research_workflow(topic, client=client)
        report_path = save_report(result, output_dir=output_dir)
    except (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError) as error:
        print(f"\nWorkflow failed; no completed report was saved: {error}")
        return 1
    print("\nFinal Revised Brief (unverified draft)")
    print("=" * 45)
    print(result.final_brief)
    print(f"\nFull workflow report saved to: {report_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from workflow import ResearchWorkflowResult
from report_writer import slugify, build_markdown_report, save_report


def sample_result() -> ResearchWorkflowResult:
    return ResearchWorkflowResult(
        topic="Agentic AI With Python", plan="Plan content", research_notes="Research notes",
        draft="Draft brief", review="Reviewer feedback", final_brief="Final brief",
    )


def test_slugify():
    # The source's expected "python_ai_agents" belongs to different input words.
    assert slugify("Agentic AI With Python!") == "agentic_ai_with_python"


def test_slugify_empty_text():
    assert slugify("!!!") == "research_brief"


def test_build_markdown_report_contains_all_sections():
    report = build_markdown_report(sample_result())
    for text in (
        "# Research Workflow Report", "Agentic AI With Python", "Plan content", "Research notes",
        "Draft brief", "Reviewer feedback", "Final brief", "Important Verification Note",
    ):
        assert text in report


def test_slug_preserves_other_topic_and_collapses_separators():
    assert slugify("Python AI agents") == "python_ai_agents"
    assert slugify("  AI--with__Python  ") == "ai_with_python"
    assert slugify("abcdefgh", max_length=4) == "abcd"
    assert "/" not in slugify("../../private/file")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("limit", [0, -1, True, 2.5])
def test_slug_rejects_invalid_length(limit):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="positive integer"):
        slugify("example", limit)


def test_nested_save_does_not_overwrite_and_preserves_markdown(tmp_path):
    result = sample_result()
    result.final_brief = "## Revised\n\n- Item\n\n```python\nprint('hello')\n```"
    target = tmp_path / "new" / "nested" / "reports"
    first = save_report(result, str(target))
    second = save_report(result, str(target))
    assert isinstance(first, Path)
    assert first.parent == second.parent == target
    assert first != second
    assert first.read_text() == second.read_text() == build_markdown_report(result)
    assert result.final_brief in first.read_text()


def test_model_reviewer_cannot_record_human_approval():
    result = sample_result()
    result.review = "Recommendation: publish. Everything is verified."
    report = build_markdown_report(result)
    assert "Status: Unverified model draft. No human approval has been recorded." in report
    assert "A model review is not factual verification or permission to publish." in report
    assert result.review in report  # Retained as model feedback, not promoted to an approval flag.

9.18 File: README.md

# Research and Summary Agent

This independent Chapter 9 project runs five roles in order:
Planner → Researcher → Writer → Reviewer → Reviser. It saves the topic and all
five outputs in a Markdown report so you can inspect their hand-offs.

The researcher uses model-generated notes. It does not browse, retrieve sources
or verify current claims. A reviewer recommendation to publish is still model
text; it never records human approval or changes the report's unverified status.

## Setup

Use Python 3.10 or newer. Create a separate environment in this project directory:

```sh
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

On Windows PowerShell, replace the activation command with:

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

## Run offline checks

```sh
python -m pytest -q
```

Tests use fixture model responses at the client boundary. The Python role
functions, five-step orchestration, validation, CLI entrypoint and report writes
actually run. No API key or network model call is needed. These tests do not
measure a live model's writing quality or factual accuracy.

## Run with a live model

Only this step requires credentials and can incur provider charges:

```sh
cp .env.example .env
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

Set your own key in `.env`, keeping that file private. The default model remains
`gpt-4.1-mini`, with temperature `0.2`. Then run:

```sh
python app.py
```

Example topics:

- Python AI agents for freelancers
- How RAG improves document assistants
- Benefits and risks of AI workflow automation
- How small businesses can use AI assistants

A successful workflow makes five model requests. Empty responses and provider
errors stop it; they do not create a completed report. Each successful save uses
a UTC timestamp and unique suffix under `outputs/`, so repeated runs do not
overwrite earlier reports. Nested output directories are supported.

## Files and interfaces

- `llm_client.py`: `LLMClient.complete(system, user)` lazily connects; an injected
  SDK-compatible client enables offline tests. Role instructions use the
  Responses API's `instructions` field, separate from user content.
- `prompts.py`: the original five prompt builders and their role instructions.
- `agents.py`: the five agent functions accept an optional keyword-only `client`.
- `workflow.py`: `run_research_workflow(topic, client=...)` shares that client and
  validates each stage before continuing.

9.19 How the Code Works

The workflow calls five agent functions in order and passes one shared client through the sequence. The excerpts below use the cleaned_topic, client and stage outputs created in run_research_workflow(); they are parts of that function, not standalone scripts. If a stage fails or returns no usable text, later stages do not run.

Agent 1: Planner

The planner receives the topic and identifies what the brief should explore.

plan = planner_agent(cleaned_topic, client=client)

Its output sets the scope for the next step; it is not the finished brief.

Agent 2: Researcher

The researcher uses the topic and plan to organise notes.

research_notes = researcher_agent(
    topic=cleaned_topic,
    plan=plan,
    client=client,
)

The prompt contains four explicit limits:

Do not pretend you browsed the web.

Do not invent statistics.

Do not invent citations.

Mark uncertain or current claims as "Needs verification."

These instructions establish the intended behaviour. Check whether the notes actually follow them.

Agent 3: Writer

The writer turns the notes into a structured brief for the target reader.

draft = writer_agent(
    topic=cleaned_topic,
    research_notes=research_notes,
    client=client,
)

Agent 4: Reviewer

The reviewer examines that draft:

review = reviewer_agent(draft, client=client)

It looks for unsupported claims, vague wording, missing context, overpromising, confusing structure and claims that require verification. This is an editorial and factual-risk check, not a check against external sources.

Agent 5: Reviser

The reviser receives both the draft and the review.

final_brief = reviser_agent(
    draft=draft,
    review=review,
    client=client,
)

Compare the revision with the draft. It should address the feedback while retaining necessary uncertainty and avoiding new unsupported claims.

9.20 Why Save Intermediate Outputs?

The report keeps the Research Plan, Research Notes, Draft Brief, Reviewer Feedback and Final Revised Brief. Together they show how the answer developed. Each report begins with an unverified-draft notice: a model reviewer cannot record human approval. Saves create missing parent directories and use a UTC timestamp plus a unique suffix, so a new run does not overwrite an earlier report.

When a final brief is weak, work through those stages. Check whether the plan was too broad, the notes lacked detail, the writer ignored risks or the reviewer overlooked a problem. Also check that the reviser did not add a claim absent from the evidence. A saved Markdown report gives this small project a useful form of observability: you can inspect what happened between the input and final output.

9.24 Debugging Multi-Step Workflows

Start with the stage immediately before a visible failure. A poor final brief may originate in the research notes or plan, so changing only the final prompt can leave the underlying problem untouched. Use the saved stages to identify the first point where the output departs from what you intended.

9.25 When Multi-Agent Workflows Help

Separate roles can be useful for tasks with distinct phases, especially when a draft benefits from a second pass. Examples include research briefs, proposals, reports, content plans, code review, product analysis, customer feedback analysis, business workflow drafts and educational lessons.

A reviewer may notice something the writer missed. Assess that benefit on your own examples before making the extra call a permanent part of the application.

9.26 When Multi-Agent Workflows Are Overkill

Simple rewriting, short summaries, one-line answers, basic classification and small formatting tasks often need only one call. Simple maths and tasks that ordinary Python handles reliably may need none.

For example:

Convert this title to lowercase.

Use the string method:

title.lower()

A five-role workflow would add cost and complexity without helping this task.

9.27 Cost and Latency Considerations

This workflow makes a planner call, researcher call, writer call, reviewer call and reviser call. One user request therefore becomes five model calls, increasing the amount of processing and usually the wait for a response.

  • Try smaller models for planning or review where their results meet your needs.
  • Limit output length and start prompt experiments with short topics.
  • Save intermediate outputs and cache results that can be reused.
  • Rerun only the stage that needs improvement when the earlier inputs remain suitable.
  • Keep extra stages only where they make a useful difference.

Some applications need just two steps, such as Draft → Review or Analyze → Write. Choose the shortest workflow that handles the task well.

Load relevant preferences after receiving the topic. The planner and researcher create their outputs, the writer uses the preferences while drafting, and the reviewer checks the result. Pass memory only to stages that need it; unrelated details can distract from the current task.

9.30 Adding RAG to This Workflow

RAG can give the researcher approved source material to work from. The planner first creates questions, retrieval returns relevant source chunks, and the researcher summarises that context. The writer then drafts the brief, and the reviewer checks how well its claims are supported by the retrieved material.

This is a useful extension for internal reports, policies, meeting notes, product docs, customer feedback and research libraries. Its reliability still depends on retrieving suitable material and using it accurately. Source context gives you something to check; it does not automatically make every resulting statement correct.

9.33 Common Mistakes

1. Using Too Many Agents

Define the job of each role before adding it. Remove a stage if it repeats work without improving the result.

2. Giving Agents Overlapping Roles

If the researcher writes the entire article and the writer starts again, the hand-off is unclear. Specify what each stage should receive and produce.

3. Not Saving Intermediate Outputs

Keep the plan, notes, draft, review and revision so you can locate errors and compare changes.

4. Claiming Facts Have Been Verified

This workflow does not consult outside sources. Keep uncertainty labels and verify factual claims separately.

5. Skipping the Reviewer Without Assessing Its Use

A reviewer can identify unclear writing and weak claims. Check its contribution on examples, and remember that it can also miss mistakes.

6. Letting the Reviser Add New Claims

Compare the revision with its inputs. Improved wording should not introduce facts that the notes cannot support.

7. Ignoring Cost

Track the cost of the whole sequence, including repeated runs. Five calls need to justify the additional work.

9.34 Best Practices

Keep roles focused and the workflow simple enough to inspect. Save intermediate results, use tools and memory only where they serve the current step, and add RAG when the task needs approved source material.

Retain a review step where it helps, mark uncertain claims, and check the final output before publication. Instructions against invented citations or statistics are useful constraints, but the resulting text still needs examination.

9.35 Mini Challenges

Challenge 1: Add a Critic Score

Ask the reviewer to score the draft from 1 to 10 for clarity, usefulness, factual risk, structure and reader fit. Treat these as the reviewer's judgements, not measured accuracy scores.

Challenge 2: Add a Short Brief Mode

Let the user choose short, medium or detailed, then adjust the writer prompt.

Challenge 3: Add a Source-Grounded Mode

Connect the semantic search from Chapter 5 so that the researcher retrieves local notes before preparing its own notes.

Challenge 4: Add Memory Preferences

Use Chapter 7 memory to store a writing preference, such as:

The user prefers brief executive summaries.

Challenge 5: Add a Human Approval Step

As an optional exercise, ask whether to save the local draft. A yes/no save choice is not factual verification or permission to publish:

Save final report? yes/no

Challenge 6: Add a Second Reviewer

Create clarity_reviewer and risk_reviewer, then combine their feedback. Compare the result and cost with the single-reviewer version.

9.36 Chapter Summary

The project divides brief-writing into planning, research notes, drafting, review and revision. Each role has a specific input and output, and the saved Markdown report lets you inspect the full sequence.

You have also identified the limits of that structure. More calls can increase cost and repeat errors; a polished revision can still contain unverified claims. The next chapter develops input checks, output validation and review boundaries for these and the earlier projects.

Key Takeaways

  • Multi-step workflows organise work into stages; role-based agents give those stages separate instructions.
  • Intermediate outputs help you trace a problem to its source.
  • A model reviewer can identify weaknesses but cannot substitute for evidence-based verification.
  • Choose the fewest stages that meet the task's needs, and account for the cost of the full sequence.
  • A portfolio should show how the workflow operates and where its limits remain.
